title: Where to Start When Your AI Agent Isn't Performing
author: Jason D.
excerpt: A practical guide to diagnosing underperforming AI agents. Before you retrain, rebuild, or blame the model, start with your evaluation framework.
content:
You shipped an AI agent. It passed QA. The demo looked great. But in production, accuracy is hovering around 70%, and your operations team is spending more time babysitting the agent than doing the work manually.

Sound familiar? You're not alone. According to Gartner, 95% of enterprises run AI pilots, but only 11% make it to production with consistent results.

Step 1: Don't Blame the Model

The instinct is always to retrain, swap models, or add more data. Resist it. In our experience, underperformance is rarely a model problem. It's almost always one of these:

  • Unclear success criteria — What does "good" look like? If you can't define it precisely, you can't measure it.
  • Missing evaluation framework — Without automated evals, you're guessing. Vibes don't scale.
  • Data quality issues — The model is only as good as what you feed it. Garbage in, garbage out.
  • Edge case blindness — The 95% case works fine. The 5% is where trust dies.

Step 2: Build Your Evaluation Framework First

Before touching the model, build the measurement system. An evaluation framework should include:

evaluation_framework/
├── accuracy_metrics.py      # Task-specific accuracy
├── edge_case_tests.py      # Known failure scenarios
├── regression_suite.py     # Catch regressions early
├── latency_benchmarks.py   # Response time tracking
└── confidence_scoring.py   # When to escalate to humans

This gives you a baseline. Every change you make from here can be measured against it.

Step 3: Trace the Failures

Collect traces of every agent interaction. Look for patterns in the failures:

  • Are failures clustered around specific input types?
  • Is there a time-of-day pattern (suggesting data staleness)?
  • Are certain edge cases appearing more frequently than expected?
  • Is the agent confident when it's wrong (calibration issue)?

The fastest path to a better agent isn't more training data. It's better visibility into where and why it fails.

Step 4: Fix the Pipeline, Not the Prompt

Most "prompt engineering" is duct tape. Instead of tweaking prompts endlessly, invest in the pipeline:

  • Better input validation and preprocessing
  • Structured output parsing with fallbacks
  • Confidence thresholds that route uncertain cases to humans
  • Monitoring that alerts before accuracy degrades

The Bottom Line

An underperforming AI agent is a systems problem, not a model problem. Start with evaluation, trace your failures, and fix the pipeline. The model is rarely the bottleneck — your ability to measure and iterate is.
